# latex-look — teach an agent to *see* your LaTeX
**English** · 简体中文

*Left: compiles with zero errors. Right: after five sentences a reader could say out
loud — "remove

the rules around the title", "this table is a grid, make it a
booktabs table", "that link runs off t

he page", "the figure is too wide". Try it
yourself in `examples/broken-layout`.*
A **DeepSeek Harness plugin** that adds exactly one tool: `latex_look`.
An agent that only reads `.tex` source is blind: a document can compile with zero errors and still l
ook wrong. `latex_look` compiles the document, renders the page as an image, maps any spot on that p
age back to the exact source line, and diffs what your last edit changed — in a single call.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
**Read the case study:** a 215-page LaTeX book, read the way a reader reads it — 163 figures, 129 eq
uations, six classes of defect that compile cleanly.
## Why one tool, not three
Rendering, locating, and diffing are the *implementation*. The agent needs one coherent verb — **"lo
ok at this page"** — the same way a person does. `latex_look` compiles, renders, resolves, and diffs
in a single call, so the loop is:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Install
Requires Node ≥ 18, a TeX engine (`xelatex`/`lualatex`/`pdflatex`/`latexmk` or tectonic), `synctex`,
a TeX engine (`xelatex`/`lualatex`/`pdflatex`/`latexmk` or tectonic), `synctex`, and `ghostscript`.
This repository **is** the bundle: `package.json` declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, and `cordis.patch.yml
is** the bundle: `package.json` declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, and `cordis.patch.yml` inserts one row.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Then install it into the current profile (in the Harness, via the plugin manager):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
That adds the row `latex-look` and registers the `latex_look` tool. Replacing the sources of an alre
ady-installed package needs a Harness restart to load a fresh module generation.
Published on npm as `@fffangchenghao/dsh-latex-look`, so the same row also installs straight from th
n npm as `@fffangchenghao/dsh-latex-look`, so the same row also installs straight from the registry:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### Updating

Two different facts, and the plugin reports them separately because confusing them is
how an update

facts, and the plugin reports them separately because confusing them is
how an update goes missing:

**A newer release exists.** The registry is asked once a day, in the background; when
something newe

r is published, one line is appended to a tool reply. An offline machine
sees nothing at all, and an
unreachable registry is never reported as "up to date".

**A newer release is already installed.** This is the one that silently bites. An
updater replaces t

he package directory while the old code keeps running, so the
running code goes on reading its versi

on out of a `package.json` that was swapped
underneath it — it reports the *new* number while execut

ing the *old* code, and
everything looks current. The plugin therefore remembers the version it star

ted with,
re-reads the disk at most once a minute, and when the two disagree says so:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The plugin does not update itself. Replacing the files of a running process is the
profile's job, no

t a tool's: an updater plugin already installed in the profile does
it, or you do it by hand. When t

he plugin can tell which profile it was installed
into, it prints the exact command — the profile na

me is read off its own path,
because they are called `desktop` and `web` and a guess sends you to an

install that
does nothing:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`core.mjs` is not hot-reloaded, so a plugin update takes effect on the next start of
the harness, ne

t hot-reloaded, so a plugin update takes effect on the next start of
the harness, never mid-session.
From a checkout, both questions are available directly:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### Releasing
Tagging `v*` runs the test suite on Ubuntu with TeX and Ghostscript installed, verifies the tag matc
hes `package.json`, and publishes to npm. The token comes from the `NPM_TOKEN` repository secret.
### Optional: the knowledge skill
The tool gives the agent eyes. `SKILL.md` gives it the LaTeX knowledge to act on what it sees — a sy
mptom → cause → fix playbook (a rule you want gone is usually `\pagestyle`/`fancyhdr`, not a stray `
\hline`). Copy or symlink it into the skills root:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### CLI, for humans and for testing
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The CLI runs the same engine as the plugin and needs no Harness, which makes it the fast way to chec
k a change without reloading anything.
### MCP server, for Claude Desktop, Cursor and Codex

The same engine ships as a Model Context Protocol server, so a client that has never
heard of DSH ca

n use it. It is the same `look()` and the same words in the reply — the
plugin is the Harness shape,
this is the universal one.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Put that in `claude_desktop_config.json` (Claude Desktop), `~/.cursor/mcp.json`
(Cursor), or as a TO
ML block in `~/.codex/config.toml`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

It exposes one tool, `latex_look`, with the same parameters as everywhere else:
`file`, `page`, `tex

t`, `pointX`/`pointY`, `compare`, `audit`, `sequence`, `dpi`.
Pages come back as image content block
s, so the model sees the page itself.
Requirements are the usual ones — a TeX engine and `ghostscript` on `PATH`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

On Windows nothing has to be added to `PATH`: the plugin asks for `gswin64c`
(that is Ghostscript's

real name there), and when that is not found it looks in
`C:\Program Files\gs\gs*\bin`, plus the TeX

Live, MiKTeX and TinyTeX install
directories. If you would rather be explicit, point `PATH` at
`C:\
Program Files\gs\gs10.05.1\bin` and it is used first.
Nothing is uploaded: every call compiles the document that is already on your disk.
Listed in the official MCP Registry as `io.github.fangchenghao/latex-look`, so clients that search t
he registry can install it by name, and on awesome-mcp-servers.
